questions.question_text: The coordination number for tetrahedral complexes is ---- .
questions.answer: The coordination number for a tetrahedral complex is 4 because there are four ligand atoms directly bonded to the central metal ion.

questions.question_text: The crystal field theory considers the metal-ligand bond to be a ______ bond.
questions.answer: Crystal field theory models the interaction between metal and ligands as purely electrostatic (ionic) in nature.

questions.question_text: Transition metals are generally coloured because ----- .
options: their penultimate d-subshells are fully filled
questions.answer: Colour in transition metals arises due to d-d electron transitions, where electrons jump between d orbitals of different energy.
questions.chapter: Unit 1: Optical & magnetic properties of transition metal complexes

questions.question_text: Which of the following complexes has a magnetic moment of 1.73 BM?
questions.answer: [Cu(NH3)4]2+ has one unpaired electron, resulting in a magnetic moment of approximately 1.73 Bohr Magneton (BM).
questions.chapter: Unit 1: Optical & magnetic properties of transition metal complexes

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a thermodynamic function?
questions.answer: Frictional energy is not a state function in thermodynamics, unlike internal energy, enthalpy and entropy.

questions.question_text: In an electrochemical corrosion ------ .
questions.answer: In electrochemical corrosion, oxidation occurs at the anode leading to metal dissolution.

questions.question_text: The solubility product increases with an increase in ------------ .
questions.answer: Most salts have higher solubility at higher temperatures, so their solubility product (Ksp) increases with temperature.

questions.question_text: When an equilibrium is reached inside the two half-cells of an electrochemical cell, what is the net voltage across the electrodes?
questions.answer: At equilibrium, the cell potential becomes zero because the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal.
questions.chapter: Unit 2: Use of free energy in chemical equilibria

questions.question_text: Enantiomers are ---- .
options: Molecules that have a mirror image
Molecules that have at least one stereogenic center
Non-superimposable molecules that are mirror images of each other
questions.answer: Enantiomers are stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other.

questions.question_text: The plane that divides the molecule into two equal parts so that each half is the mirror image of the other half is called as ---- .
questions.answer: Plane of symmetry is an imaginary plane dividing the molecule into two mirror-image halves.

questions.question_text: How many optical isomers are possible in a compound with one chiral carbon?
questions.answer: A single chiral carbon can give rise to two non-superimposable mirror images, i.e., two optical isomers.

questions.question_text: The potential energy of n-butane is minimum for ----- conformation.
questions.answer: The staggered conformation is the most stable as steric repulsion is minimized, leading to lowest potential energy.

questions.question_text: In addition polymers, monomers used are ----- .
questions.answer: Addition polymerization requires monomers with double or triple bonds, i.e., unsaturated compounds.

questions.question_text: The polymer in which the substituents are sterically arranged in a way to give alternate d and l configuration is known as --- .
questions.answer: Syndiotactic polymers have substituents arranged in an alternating fashion along the polymer backbone.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true for the resultant polymer product formed, when molecules of pthalic acid react with molecules of glycerol?
questions.answer: The reaction between polyfunctional monomers like phthalic acid and glycerol results in a crosslinked structure.

questions.question_text: Which among following is a naturally occurring polymer?
questions.answer: Proteins are natural polymers composed of amino acids; the others are synthetic or not polymers.

questions.question_text: Hooke's law essentially defines ----.
questions.answer: Hooke's law describes the linear relationship between stress and strain, up to the elastic limit.

questions.question_text: Composites can be classified based on ------ .
options: Neither on matrix type nor on reinforcement constituent type
questions.answer: Composites are commonly classified based on both their matrix material and the type of reinforcement.

questions.question_text: ESCA can identify elements in the periodic table above which of the following?
questions.answer: ESCA (XPS) can identify all elements above helium, but not hydrogen or helium themselves.

questions.question_text: With the help of which of the following equations the interplanar distance can be calculated from a known wavelength of the source and measured angle?
questions.answer: Bragg's law is used in XRD to calculate the distance between crystal planes from the wavelength and diffraction angle.
